subject.title: fix(qqbot): allow approval buttons in direct C2C conversations

question: Which QQBot identity should be trusted to approve privileged operations in direct C2C conversations when `execApprovals` is absent?
rationale: The patch assumes every direct callback actor is trusted, but open DM policy and the existing attacker-versus-owner authorization contract make that a security-policy choice rather than a safe mechanical bypass.

options.title: Require trusted owner identity
options.body: Authorize only a callback sender matching an active-config approver or another platform-proven bot-owner identity.

options.title: Trust every C2C sender
options.body: Accept the unconditional bypass only if maintainers confirm that all QQBot direct senders are allowed to approve privileged operations.

options.title: Require execApprovals
options.body: Keep fallback direct approvals fail-closed unless an explicit `execApprovals` policy identifies approvers.

recommendation.title: Require trusted owner identity
recommendation.body: Authorize only a callback sender matching an active-config approver or another platform-proven bot-owner identity.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged authorization work established and proved the current attacker-versus-owner security boundary.
